findings.rationale: Local performance is well off the federation: round-20 AUC 0.5555 vs pooled 0.7655, ECE 0.2143, CITL -0.1987 (mean predicted 0.16 vs observed prevalence 0.358, while the pooled prevalence is 0.156). The observed prevalence is about 0.33-0.38 in every round from round 1 (c9), with no feature drift (shift_sd near 0 in most rounds). The prevalence is too high for the features, and discrimination is badly reduced, which fits flipped outcome labels rather than a clean prevalence shift. Subgroup O/E is elevated uniformly across sex groups (2.35 and 2.07), so this is not subgroup-specific under-diagnosis. Its updates are also anomalous (mean cos -0.86 against the median, norm ratio about 7 vs median), consistent with a client training away from the federation on corrupted labels.

Round-20 AUC 0.5721 vs pooled 0.7655, ECE 0.2099, CITL -0.2095 (mean predicted 0.141 vs observed prevalence 0.351). The prevalence is about 0.32-0.39 in every round from round 1 with no feature drift (c9), so the excess positives are present from the start and the labels, not the features, look wrong. Subgroup O/E is high in all sex, age and income groups (for example 2.91 for sex 0 and 2.37 for sex 1), so the inflation is not confined to one subgroup. Its updates are strongly anti-aligned with the median (mean cos -0.86, norm ratio about 7.5).

Round-20 AUC 0.584 vs pooled 0.7655, ECE 0.1897, CITL -0.1925 (mean predicted 0.167 vs observed prevalence 0.359). The prevalence is about 0.27-0.57 across rounds from round 1 with no feature drift, and the excess positives are not explained by the features. Subgroup O/E is elevated in both sex groups (2.01 and 2.12), which points to label corruption rather than subgroup-specific under-diagnosis. Its updates are anti-aligned with the median (mean cos -0.85, norm ratio about 4.7).

report.summary: Screened all 52 clients with client_updates, client_performance, drift_by_round, feature_summary, and subgroup_outcomes (Sex, AgeGroup, Income), plus attribution_churn for explanation stability. Three clients (NE, NY, SC) stand far apart from the rest on several independent screens. Each shows a very low local AUC (0.56-0.58 vs pooled 0.77), an observed prevalence around 0.35 against roughly 0.15 implied by its features (CITL around -0.2), and updates anti-aligned with the median, with a size-adjusted norm far above the median. Their prevalence is elevated from round 1 with no feature drift, and O/E is inflated uniformly across subgroups, so I classify them as label_noise from onset round 1. I did not flag other clients. Single outliers at ND (HighChol sd), NC (GenHlth p99), and ND/NC re-checks came back normal on narrower re-query and were treated as noise. GU shows an erratic per-round update pattern (mean cos 0.23, z about -4.4), but it is a small client (n=708) and its deviations fall below the threshold, so I did not report it. No client showed a clear explanation-instability or missing-artefact signature. Budget was nearly fully used (19.5 of 20 spent).
